Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: calibration-set-representativeness-first - the single largest hidden variable in a weight-only quantization (WOQ) comparison is the calibration set, not the bit width. GPTQ/AWQ-style methods solve a per-layer reconstruction objective against activations sampled from a calibration corpus; if that corpus is generic web text while production traffic is code or tool-call JSON, the per-channel scales are fitted to the wrong activation distribution and quality regresses on exactly the traffic you care about.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: with calibration drawn from a held-out sample of production traffic, INT4 WOQ accuracy delta versus BF16 on the production task suite is <=1 absolute point, and this delta is strictly smaller than the delta obtained with a generic-web calibration set.

Controlled experiment: Freeze model weights, tokenizer, prompt set, sampling params (greedy, temperature 0, fixed seed), engine version and GPU type. Vary exactly one factor: calibration corpus (generic vs production-sampled), holding sample count and sequence length fixed. Quantize twice, evaluate both on the same held-out production eval set that shares no prompts with calibration.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Calibration sample count and max sequence length silently change group-wise scale statistics; sampling nondeterminism; eval set leakage into calibration; different quantization group sizes (g128 vs g64) being changed at the same time as the corpus.

corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: numerical-outlier-and-activation-range-first - WOQ quality loss is dominated by a small number of outlier activation channels, so a fair comparison must characterise the activation range before it reports a cost number. A model whose activations are well conditioned will tolerate INT4 group-wise quantization with near-zero loss; a model with heavy-tailed channels will collapse at exactly the layers that carry long-range attention structure.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: layers whose per-channel activation kurtosis exceeds a fixed threshold account for the majority of the accuracy delta, such that keeping those layers in higher precision recovers >=80% of the lost accuracy at <10% of the memory saving given back.

Controlled experiment: Instrument a BF16 forward pass over the calibration corpus and record per-channel activation max and kurtosis per linear layer. Rank layers, build three artefacts: all-INT4, INT4-with-top-k-outlier-layers-in-INT8, and BF16 baseline. Evaluate all three on the identical eval harness and identical hardware.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Outlier statistics depend on the corpus used to collect them; per-tensor versus per-channel scaling conflated with bit width; some kernels silently upcast, hiding the effect.

Analytical stance under test: kernel-autotuning-and-gemm-shape-first - a WOQ cost claim is a kernel claim. The dequantize-then-GEMM path only wins when the GEMM is memory-bandwidth bound, which is the decode phase at small batch. At large batch or during prefill the GEMM is compute bound and the dequantization overhead can make INT4 slower than BF16 on the same hardware. Reporting a single throughput number without stating batch size and phase is not a comparison.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: INT4 WOQ improves decode-phase tokens/sec at batch<=8 by a measurable margin, and shows no improvement or a regression in prefill-dominated throughput at batch>=64.

Controlled experiment: Sweep batch size across a fixed grid, separating prefill and decode timing with engine-level instrumentation rather than end-to-end latency. Fix sequence lengths, GPU clocks (lock via nvidia-smi -lgc), and engine version. Run the autotuner to convergence for both dtypes so neither is handicapped by an unwarmed kernel cache.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Cold autotune cache making the first configuration look slow; GPU clock throttling across a long sweep; CUDA graph capture enabled for one dtype only; different tensor-parallel degrees.

corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: cost-model-and-unit-economics-first - the stated goal is lower serving cost, so the comparison must terminate in cost per million output tokens at a fixed SLO, not in tokens/sec. Throughput gains that require violating the p99 latency target are not cost savings, and memory savings only become cost savings if they let you either raise concurrency on the same GPU count or retire GPUs entirely.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: at a fixed p99 TTFT and p99 TPOT SLO, INT4 WOQ reduces cost per million output tokens by a margin larger than the measurement noise band, on the production arrival process.

Controlled experiment: Define the SLO first. For each dtype, run a load sweep and find the maximum sustainable request rate that holds the SLO. Convert to cost using GPU-hour price and measured achieved rate. Replay a captured production arrival trace rather than a uniform load generator, since burstiness changes the achievable rate.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Uniform closed-loop load generators overstate achievable rate; ignoring the accuracy delta means comparing two different products; amortised quantization and re-validation engineering cost omitted.

Analytical stance under test: long-context-and-kv-dominance-first - WOQ shrinks weights, not the KV cache. At long context the KV cache dominates memory, so weight-only quantization delivers a shrinking marginal benefit as sequence length grows. Compute achievable concurrency at each length under a fixed memory budget. Hold batch policy and paging block size constant.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Paged attention block size and preemption policy changing between runs; workspace buffers scaling with batch; measuring reserved rather than allocated memory.

If the accuracy difference of interest is one absolute point on a benchmark of a few hundred items, the binomial standard error alone is comparable to the effect, so a point-estimate table is uninformative. corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: accuracy-metric-selection-and-task-sensitivity-first - quantization damage is not uniform across task types. Perplexity is the least sensitive metric and is routinely used to declare quantization harmless; structured generation, long chain-of-thought arithmetic, and tool-call argument fidelity are far more sensitive because a single altered token can invalidate an entire output. A fair comparison picks metrics matched to the failure modes quantization actually produces.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: perplexity delta between BF16 and INT4 understates the regression measured on strict-format tool-call validity by a factor large enough that perplexity alone would have passed an artefact that the strict metric rejects.

Controlled experiment: Score both artefacts on a metric ladder: perplexity, multiple-choice accuracy, exact-match generation, and strict schema-validated tool-call success. Use the identical prompt set and identical decoding across the ladder. Report each rung separately and never aggregate them into one score.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Different decoding parameters per metric; lenient parsers rescuing malformed outputs and masking the regression; benchmark contamination.

Analytical stance under test: hardware-generation-and-dtype-support-first - the result is only valid for the GPU generation it was measured on. INT4 WOQ performance depends on whether the hardware and kernel stack have native support for the required dequantize and MMA paths; on an Ampere-class card such as A30 there is no FP8 tensor-core path and INT4 relies on dequantize-to-FP16 GEMM, whereas Hopper-class parts can take a different and faster route. Publishing a single speedup ratio without naming the GPU is an unfalsifiable claim.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: the INT4-versus-BF16 speedup ratio differs materially between the two GPU generations available to the team, such that a decision made on one generation would be wrong on the other.

Controlled experiment: Run the identical harness, engine version, and model on each GPU generation in the fleet. Record compute capability, driver, CUDA and engine versions per run. Report the ratio per generation and never average across generations.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Different driver or engine versions across the two machines; different memory bandwidth and clock ceilings conflated with dtype effect; one generation falling back to a reference kernel.

Analytical stance under test: reproducibility-and-artefact-provenance-first - a fair comparison is one someone else can rerun and get the same answer. That requires the quantization run itself to be a recorded, hashed, reproducible artefact: quantization method and version, group size, bit width, calibration corpus hash, seed, and the resulting checkpoint hash. Without this, a later regression cannot be attributed to the quantization step versus everything else that changed.

Falsifiable hypothesis (H0): H0: an independent rerun of the recorded quantization recipe reproduces a checkpoint whose evaluation results fall within the measurement noise band of the original.

Controlled experiment: Record a full recipe manifest for each artefact. Have a second operator, on a clean checkout, rerun quantization from the manifest and re-evaluate. Compare both the checkpoint hash and the evaluation results. Treat hash mismatch with matching results as a separate, weaker pass than exact reproduction.

Confounders to hold fixed or measure: Nondeterministic quantization kernels producing hash-different but numerically equivalent checkpoints; unpinned library versions; calibration corpus mutated in place between runs.
